html:
The Rwandan Civil War began on 1 October 1990, when the Rwandan Patriotic Front, an army of mostly Tutsi exiles based in Uganda, invaded northern Rwanda.

Its leaders were children of refugees from the revolution who had fought for Yoweri Museveni in Uganda. France and Zaire helped the government stop the first attack, and Paul Kagame rebuilt the rebel army as a guerrilla force. The war hardened Hutu extremism and pushed hundreds of thousands from their homes.

A peace deal was signed at Arusha in 1993, but it collapsed in April 1994. While the genocide went on, the RPF fought its way across the country and took Kigali on 4 July. Its victory ended the war and sent the old army and militias into Zaire.
sum: The Rwandan Civil War began on 1 October 1990, when the Rwandan Patriotic Front, an army of mostly Tutsi exiles based in Uganda, invaded northern Rwanda.
